text: Olongapo City Zambales is facing widespread flooding as persistent Southwest Monsoon or Habagat rains continue to swell rivers and waterways across the city According to The Philippine Daily Inquirer floodwaters overflowed the Sta Rita and Del Rosario bridges affecting parts of Sta Rita West Bajac-Bajac East Bajac-Bajac and Kalaklan while several major roads became impassable The situation became more serious on August 29 when the Olongapo City Information Center cited by Inquirer reported that 1,395 people from 452 families were already staying in evacuation centers with other residents seeking shelter outside designated facilities Some communities experienced waist to neck-deep flooding while rescue teams were deployed to assist stranded residents The flooding was driven by continuous monsoon rains with PAGASA placing Zambales under a Red Rainfall Warning meaning serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas Authorities continue to monitor river levels and conduct rescue and evacuation operations as rain persists For many residents familiar streets and neighborhoods have temporarily turned into waterways forcing families to leave their homes and move toward safer ground The situation remains dangerous particularly near swollen rivers bridges and rapidly flowing floodwater and residents in vulnerable areas are being urged to follow evacuation orders and local disaster warnings Olongapo City Zambales
